newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's Bakonyi cuts 1996 bauxite output plan.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's Bakonyi cuts 1996 bauxite output plan.

text.p: Hungarian bauxite mining company Bakonyi Bauxitbanya Kft said it has downgraded its 1996 output plan to 1.1 million tonnes of ore from 1.3 million tonnes because it has been unable to open a new mine.

The company still hopes to start up production in Szar, near Budapest, but otherwise does not plan major expansions, Bakonyi CEO Janos Fazekas said in a telephone interview from this western Hungarian town.
"The way I see it, our production will remain at slightly above one million tonnes a year at least through the year 2000," he said.
Fazekas said Bakonyi, which is the only significant bauxite producer in Hungary with five operating mines now, wanted to put the Szar surface mine into operation earlier this year.

"The villagers in Szar are opposed to the mine, which is why we couldn't start it," he said. "But we are trying to convince them that it will cause no environmental damage, because we will clean up after we finish."
Szar is expected to produce 200,000 tonnes of ore a year for three years before it is exhausted, Fazekas added.
Other than Szar and the extension of an existing underground mine, Bakonyi does not plan major expansions, he said.

The four companies which acquired 18 percent each in Bakonyi in July - Hungary's Metalservice Kft, Magyar Aluminium Kft, Motim Kft and Fak-top Kft -- have recently agreed not to make major investments in Bakonyi to expand output, Fazekas said.
Bakonyi's owners have informed Norsk Hydro, which had urged a significant expansion, about their decision, he added.

Norsk Hydro has expressed interest in acquiring the Hungarian alumina plant Ajkai Timfoldgyar Kft when it is privatised later this year, and the Hungarian privatisation agency APV has said it is holding back 18 percent of Bakonyi to offer it to the entity that acquired Ajkai.

Norsk Hydro officials did not want to comment on the matter, saying the negotiations were ongoing, but added that their purchase of Bakonyi was conditional on ensuring a steady supply of bauxite to Ajkai.
Fazekas said Bakonyi produces more than enough bauxite for Hungary's alumina requirements, while alumina exporters could use imported bauxite.
